library(scales)
library(ggtext)
library(cowplot)

species <- c("picarus", "pargus", "csemiargus")
genomes <- c("ilPolIcar1.1", "ilPleArgu1.3", "ilCyaSemi1.1")
pops <- list()
pops[["picarus"]] <- c("ESkane2020", "Oland2020", "WSkane2020")
pops[["pargus"]] <- c("ESkane2022", "NSmaland2021", "Oland2021", "SWSkane2021")
pops[["csemiargus"]] <- c("ESkane2021", "NSmaland2021", "SESkane2022", "WSkane2021")

# read in GONE results
nes <- c()

for (i in c(1:length(species))) {
  s <- species[i]
  g <- genomes[i]
  for (p in pops[[s]]) {
    ne <- read.table(
      paste0(
        "../analyses/results/datasets/historical-",
        s,
        "-vg-notrans/analyses/gone/historical-",
        s,
        "-vg-notrans.",
        g,
        "_",
        p,
        "/Output_Ne_historical-",
        s,
        "-vg-notrans.",
        g,
        "_",
        p
      ),
      skip = 1,
      header = TRUE,
      sep = "\t"
      )
    ne$species <- s
    ne$pop <- p
    nes <- rbind(nes, ne)
  }
}


nes$year <- str_sub(nes$pop, -4, -1)
nes$region <- str_sub(nes$pop, 1, -5)

nes$species <- factor(
  nes$species,
  levels = species,
  labels = c("Po. icarus", "Pl. argus", "Cy. semiargus")
)

nes$region <- factor(
  nes$region,
  levels = c("WSkane", "SWSkane", "ESkane", "SESkane", "NSmaland", "Oland"),
  labels = c(
    "W Skåne", "SW Skåne", "E Skåne", "SE Skåne", "Småland", "Öland"
  )
)

nes$year <- nes$Generation

# P. icarus has two gens per year, so adjust for that
nes[nes$species == "Po. icarus", ]$year <- nes[nes$species == "Po. icarus", ]$Generation * 2

# plot without including first four generations, which often contain an artifact
# that causes sudden size drops
nofirst <- nes[(nes$Generation >= 5 & nes$species != "Po. icarus") | (nes$species == "Po. icarus" & nes$Generation >= 10), ] %>%
  mutate(label = if_else(Generation == 60, as.character(region), NA_character_)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Generation, y = Geometric_mean, color = region)) +
    geom_line() +
    facet_grid(cols = vars(species)) +
    scale_y_log10(labels = label_log()) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c("#244F6E", "#244F6E", "#658399", "#658399", "#8A2A3B", "#fecd03"),
      name = "Geographic Region"
    ) +
    xlim(c(0,100)) +
    xlab("Years before present") +
    ylab("Effective population size (*N~e~*)") +
    geom_label_repel(aes(label = label), nudge_x = 1, na.rm = TRUE) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "none",
      axis.title.y = element_markdown(),
      strip.text.x = element_text(face = "italic")
    )

# Same plot, but this time including those first 4 gens to compare
first <- nes %>%
  mutate(label = if_else(Generation == 60, as.character(region), NA_character_)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Generation, y = Geometric_mean, color = region)) +
    geom_line() +
    facet_grid(cols = vars(species)) +
    scale_y_log10(labels = label_log()) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c("#244F6E", "#244F6E", "#658399", "#658399", "#8A2A3B", "#fecd03"),
      name = "Geographic Region"
    ) +
    xlim(c(0,100)) +
    xlab("Years before present") +
    ylab("Effective population size (*N~e~*)") +
    geom_label_repel(aes(label = label), nudge_x = 1, na.rm = TRUE) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "none",
      axis.title.y = element_markdown(),
      strip.text.x = element_text(face = "italic")
    )

# plot both versions without and with first 4 gens for Figure S5
plot_grid(
  nofirst,
  first,
  ncol = 1,
  labels = c("A", "B")
)

title: Genetic diversity, inbreeding, and differentiation
text:
Heterozygosity (tables, statistics, and plots)
Read in heterozygosity results from genotype calls for the three species, combine them into a table and save that table for the supplement.

Individual heterozygosity table



Table 1


# prep heterozygosity dataframe and fill it in with heterozygosity estimates for
# three focal species.

hz_all <- c()

for (i in c(1:length(species))) {
  s <- species[i]
  g <- genomes[i]
  hz <- fread(
    paste0(
      "../analyses/results/datasets/historical-",
      s,
      "-vg-notrans/analyses/heterozygosity/historical-",
      s,
      "-vg-notrans.",
      g,
      "_all.dp6_allsites-filts.filtered_mindp5-allsites-jointcall_allbal0.21-0.79.notrans.fmiss0.3.bcftools.het.tsv"
    ),
    header = TRUE,
    sep = "\t"
  )
  samples <- fread(
    paste0(
      "../analyses/results/datasets/historical-",
      s,
      "-vg-notrans/qc/historical-",
      s,
      "-vg-notrans.",
      g,
      "_all.sampleqc.tsv"
    ),
    header = TRUE,
    sep = "\t",
    select = c("sample", "population", "time")
  )
  hz <- merge(hz, samples, by = "sample")
  hz$species <- s
  hz_all <- rbind(hz_all, hz)
}

# general clean up of df - separate pop name to get year and region, make
# species, time period, and region a factor with clean names

hz_all$year <- str_sub(hz_all$population, -4, -1)
hz_all$region <- str_sub(hz_all$population, 1, -5)

hz_all$species <- factor(
  hz_all$species,
  levels = species,
  labels = species_names
)

hz_all$time <- factor(
  hz_all$time,
  levels = c("historical", "modern"),
  labels = c("Historical", "Modern")
)

hz_all$region <- factor(
  hz_all$region,
  levels = c("WSkane", "SWSkane", "ESkane", "SESkane", "NSmaland", "Oland"),
  labels = c(
    "W Skåne", "SW Skåne", "E Skåne", "SE Skåne", "N Småland", "Öland"
  )
)

# repalce region name for SE/SW Skåne as they are grouped with E/W Skåne

hz_all$region_group <- hz_all$region
hz_all[hz_all$region_group == "SW Skåne", ]$region_group <- "W Skåne"
hz_all[hz_all$region_group == "SE Skåne", ]$region_group <- "E Skåne"


hz_table <- hz_all[, c(
  "sample", "species", "time", "population", "hetperbp", "hetperalt"
)]

write.table(hz_table, "../tables/hz_ests.tsv",
  row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE, sep = "\t"
)





Heterozygosity as a response to time period statistics
Run statistical tests on heterozygosity - performing LMMs with heterozygosity as a response to time period with population as a random factor. Also perform jackknifes and bootstraps to get confidence intervals around the mean estimates.

# get means and confidence intervals around mean heterozygosity using
# bootstrapping of samples

hz_means <- hz_all %>%
  group_by(species, population) %>%
  do(
    data.frame(
      rbind(
        Hmisc::smean.cl.boot(.$hetperbp, B = 1000)
      )
    )
  )

write.table(hz_means, "../tables/hz_means.tsv",
  row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE, sep = "\t"
)

# prepare table for supplement with historical/modern heterozygosity comparisons

hz_stats <- c()

for (s in species_names) {
  hist <- mean(hz_all[hz_all$species == s & hz_all$time == "Historical", ]$hetperbp * 1000)
  mod <- mean(hz_all[hz_all$species == s & hz_all$time == "Modern", ]$hetperbp * 1000)
  # estimate ratio of modern to historical heterozygosity
  ratio <- mod/hist
  # run linear mixed model with heterozygosity as response to time period and pop as a random eff.
  model <- lme(hetperbp * 1000 ~ time, random = ~1|region_group, data = hz_all[hz_all$species == s, ])
  # extract model parameter estimates with tidy
  tidyed <- tidy(model, conf.int = TRUE, effects = "fixed")
  tidydf <- tidyed[2, c(3,4,6,7,8,9)]
  tidydf$hist.mean <- hist
  # perform jackknifing as another approach to confidence intervals around means
  jackknife <- quantile(jackknife(hz_all[hz_all$species == s & hz_all$time == "Historical", ]$hetperbp * 1000, mean)$jack.values, c(0.025, 0.975))
  tidydf$hist.low.jk.ci <- jackknife[1]
  tidydf$hist.high.jk.ci <- jackknife[2]
  tidydf$mod.mean <- mod
  jackknife <- quantile(jackknife(hz_all[hz_all$species == s & hz_all$time == "Modern", ]$hetperbp * 1000, mean)$jack.values, c(0.025, 0.975))
  tidydf$mod.low.jk.ci <- jackknife[1]
  tidydf$mod.high.jk.ci <- jackknife[2]
  tidydf$`mod/hist` <- ratio
  tidydf <- round(tidydf, 5)
  tidydf$species <- s
  tidydf <- tidydf[ , c("species", "hist.mean", "hist.low.jk.ci", "hist.high.jk.ci", "mod.mean", "mod.low.jk.ci", "mod.high.jk.ci", "mod/hist", "estimate", "std.error", "statistic", "conf.low", "conf.high", "p.value")]
  hz_stats <- rbind(hz_stats, tidydf)
}

write.table(hz_stats, "../tables/hz_stats.tsv",
  row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE, sep = "\t"
)



Heterozygosity boxplots
Plot the differences in heterozygosity as a boxplot, with points colored by sampling region and time period on the y-axis.

hzbox <- ggplot(hz_all, aes(x = time, y = hetperbp * 1000)) +
  facet_grid(cols = vars(species)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    aes(x = time, y = hetperbp * 1000),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    outliers = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(color = region, shape = time),
    position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.05)
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(17, 16), guide = "none") +
  ylab("<span style='font-size: 9pt'>Heterozygous sites per 1000bp</span><br><span style='font-size: 7pt'>(excl. transitions)</span>") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = number_format(accuracy = 0.1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.20))
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("#244F6E", "#244F6E", "#658399", "#658399", "#8A2A3B", "#fecd03"),
    name = "Geographic Region"
  ) +
  geom_signif(
    data = hz_all[hz_all$species == "Cy. semiargus", ],
    comparisons = list(c("Historical", "Modern")),
    annotations="**",
    margin_top = 0,
    y_position = 3
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_markdown(),
    strip.text.x = element_text(size = 10, face = "italic")
  )

froh_all <- c()

for (i in c(1:length(species))) {

)

  "sample", "species", "time", "population", "Froh"
)]

write.table(froh_table, "../tables/froh_ests.tsv",
  row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE, sep = "\t"
)


Inbreeding coefficient as a response to time period statistics
Run statistical tests on inbreed coeff - performing LMMs with Froh as a response to time period with population as a random factor. Also perform jackknifes and bootstraps to get confidence intervals around the mean estimates. Largely the same code as heterozygosity above.

froh_means <- froh_all %>%
  group_by(species, population) %>%
  do(
    data.frame(
      rbind(
        Hmisc::smean.cl.boot(.$Froh, B = 1000)
      )
    )
  )

write.table(froh_means, "../tables/froh_means.tsv",
  row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE, sep = "\t"
)

froh_stats <- c()

for (s in species_names) {
  hist <- mean(froh_all[froh_all$species == s & froh_all$time == "Historical", ]$Froh)
  mod <- mean(froh_all[froh_all$species == s & froh_all$time == "Modern", ]$Froh)
  model <- lme(Froh ~ time, random = ~1|region_group, data = froh_all[froh_all$species == s, ])
  tidyed <- tidy(model, conf.int = TRUE, effects = "fixed")
  tidydf <- tidyed[2, c(3,4,6,7,8,9)]
  tidydf$hist.mean <- hist
  jackknife <- quantile(jackknife(froh_all[froh_all$species == s & froh_all$time == "Historical", ]$Froh, mean)$jack.values, c(0.025, 0.975))
  tidydf$hist.low.jk.ci <- jackknife[1]
  tidydf$hist.high.jk.ci <- jackknife[2]
  tidydf$mod.mean <- mod
  jackknife <- quantile(jackknife(froh_all[froh_all$species == s & froh_all$time == "Modern", ]$Froh, mean)$jack.values, c(0.025, 0.975))
  tidydf$mod.low.jk.ci <- jackknife[1]
  tidydf$mod.high.jk.ci <- jackknife[2]
  tidydf <- round(tidydf, 5)
  tidydf$species <- s
  tidydf <- tidydf[ , c(13, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 4)]
  froh_stats <- rbind(froh_stats, tidydf)
}

write.table(froh_stats, "../tables/froh_stats.tsv",
  row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE, sep = "\t"
)

Froh adjusted heterozygosity for the supplement
Combine Froh and heterozygosity tables, then use Froh to adjust heterozygosity with the equation het / (1 - Froh), which approximates the avg heterozygosity outside RoH. Plot this as a faceted boxplot for the supplement.

adj_hz <- merge(froh_all, hz_all)

# adjust heterozygosity by Froh
adj_hz$adj_hz <- adj_hz$hetperbp * 1000 / (1 - adj_hz$Froh)

roh_het <- adj_hz[ , c("sample", "population", "time", "species", "region")]
roh_het2 <- roh_het
roh_het$het <- adj_hz$hetperbp * 1000
roh_het$type <- "Including RoH"
roh_het2$het <- adj_hz$adj_hz
roh_het2$type <- "Excluding RoH"
roh_het <- rbind(roh_het, roh_het2)

roh_het$type <- factor(roh_het$type,
levels = c("Including RoH", "Excluding RoH"))

ggplot(roh_het, aes(x = time, y = het)) +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(species), cols = vars(type), scales = "free_y") +
  geom_boxplot(

Prepare a table of mean estimates of pi per population by taking means across windows. Get confidence intervals by bootstrapping across windows.

pi_all <- c()

# read in windowed pi results for population pairs
for (i in c(1:length(species))) {
  s <- species[i]
  g <- genomes[i]
  nucdiv <- fread(
    paste0(
      "../analyses/results/datasets/historical-",
      s,
      "-vg-notrans/analyses/pixy/historical-",
      s,
      "-vg-notrans.",
      g,
      "_all.dp6_allsites-filts.filtered_mindp5-allsites-jointcall_allbal0.21-0.79.notrans.fmiss0.3/pixy_pi.txt"

    header = TRUE,
    sep = "\t",
  )
  nucdiv$species <- s
  pi_all <- rbind(pi_all, nucdiv)
}

# Summarize pi results per pair, using bootstraps to get confidence intervals
pi_all <- pi_all %>%
  group_by(species, pop) %>%
  do(data.frame(rbind(Hmisc::smean.cl.boot(.$avg_pi, B = 10000))))

# Read in sampling info to group pops by

  pi_all$species,
  levels = species,
  labels = species_names
)

text:
Heterozygosity change per year
One of the metrics suggested for utilization in Sweden is the per year change in heterozygosity. While the warning categories are suggested only for significant differences, which we can’t really check with single samples per time period, we use this same calculation as it is a useful visualization.

# Calculate per species heterozygosity retention pairwise between all historical
# and modern individual pairs in each species and report a median and range

relhet_all <- c()

  for (i in seq_along(c(main_species, species))) {
    s <- c(main_species, species)[i]
    f <- c(main_species_f, species_f)[i]
    g <- c(main_genomes, genomes)[i]
    m <- c(main_species_m, species_m)[i]

    qc <- fread(
      paste0(
        "../analyses/results/datasets/historical-",
        f,
        "/qc/historical-",
        f,
        ".",
        g,
        "_all.sampleqc.tsv"
      ),
      header = TRUE,
      sep = "\t"
    )
    qc <- qc[, c("sample", "allsites-filts.depth.mean")]
    hz <- fread(
      paste0(
        "../analyses/results/datasets/historical-",
        f,
        "/analyses/heterozygosity/historical-",
        f,
        ".",
        g,
        "_all.dp6_allsites-filts.filtered_mindp5-allsites-jointcall_allbal0.21-0.79.notrans.fmiss",
        m,
        ".bcftools.het.tsv"
      ),
      header = TRUE,
      sep = "\t"
    )
    samples <- fread(
      paste0(
        "../analyses/results/datasets/historical-",
        f,
        "/poplists/historical-",
        f,
        "_all.indiv.list"
      ),
      header = TRUE,
      sep = "\t",
      select = c("sample", "population", "time", "depth")
    )
    hz <- merge(hz, samples, by = "sample")
    hz <- merge(hz, qc, by = "sample")
    if (s %in% species) {
      hz$year <- str_sub(hz$population, 1, 4)
      hz$region <- "one_region"
    } else {
      hz$year <- str_sub(hz$population, -4, -1)
      hz$region <- str_sub(hz$population, 1, -5)
      # Lump SW Skåne with W Skåne for Pl. argus
      hz[hz$region == "SWSkane", ]$region <- "WSkane"
    }
    if (nrow(hz) > 0) {
      regions <- unique(hz$region)

      relhet <- c()

      for (r in regions) {
        if (r == "SESkane") {
          historical <- hz[hz$region == "ESkane" & hz$year < 1995, ]$sample
        } else {
          historical <- hz[hz$region == r & hz$year < 1995, ]$sample
        }
        modern <- hz[hz$region == r & hz$year > 1995, ]$sample
        if (length(historical) > 0 & length(modern) > 0) {
          combos <- expand.grid(historical, modern)
          colnames(combos) <- c("historical", "modern")
          combos <- merge(
            combos,
            hz[, c("sample", "hetperbp", "year")],
            by.x = "historical", by.y = "sample"
          )
          colnames(combos) <- c("historical", "modern", "histhz", "histyear")
          combos <- merge(
            combos,
            hz[, c("sample", "hetperbp", "year")],
            by.x = "modern", by.y = "sample"
          )
          colnames(combos) <- c(
            "historical", "modern", "histhz", "histyear", "modhz",
            "modyear"
          )
          # below is the main estimate of heterozygosity retention per year
          combos$histyear <- as.numeric(combos$histyear)
          combos$modyear <- as.numeric(combos$modyear)
          combos$het_retained <- (combos$modhz / combos$histhz)
          combos$het_retained_peryear <- exp(
            log(combos$het_retained) / (combos$modyear - combos$histyear)
          )
          combos$rel_delta_het <- combos$het_retained - 1
          combos$rel_delta_het_peryear <- combos$het_retained_peryear - 1
          combos$pred_het_ret_100 <- (combos$het_retained_peryear^100) * 100
          if (s %in% c(
            "aagestis", "cminimus", "palcon", "pamandus", "pargyrognomon"
          )) {
            r <- "WSkane"
          } else if (s == "aoptilete") {
            r <- "NSmaland"
          } else if (s == "cargiolus") {
            r <- "Oland"
          }
          combos$region <- r
          combos$species <- s
          relhet_all <- rbind(relhet_all, combos)
          relhet_all$historical <- as.character(relhet_all$historical)
          relhet_all$modern <- as.character(relhet_all$modern)
        } else {
          df <- data.frame(
            "hist", "mod", 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, "other_region", s
          )
          colnames(df) <- colnames(relhet_all)
          relhet_all <- rbind(relhet_all, df)
        }
      }
    } else {
      df <- data.frame(
        "hist", "mod", 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, "other_region", s
      )
      colnames(df) <- colnames(relhet_all)
      relhet_all <- rbind(relhet_all, df)
    }
  }

relhet_meds <- relhet_all %>%
  group_by(species, region) %>%
  summarise(
    med = median(pred_het_ret_100),
    min = min(pred_het_ret_100),
    max = max(pred_het_ret_100)
  )

title: Putatively deleterious mutation burden
text:
Putatively deleterious mutation burden

Derived count statistics and table
In this study as a genomic proxy for genetic load, we used the derived count of putatively deleterious mutations. The main workflow provides this output as a table of derived allele counts at different position categories, including counts in homozygous state in particular. We first compile these counts into derived counts / 1000 genotyped positions to make them comparable across samples with variable missingness. We calculate means of these counts for each mutation category both for the total count and homozygous count. Then we performa linear mixed models with derived count as a response to sampling time period, with sampling region as a random factor. We also get confidence intervals around the mean counts with jackknifing.

# read in the derived count tables as output by the workflow, using the one
# that is polarized by the inferred ancestral states. read in Froh estimates
# as well to associate them later
varcounts_all <- c()
froh_all <- c()

for (i in c(1:length(species))) {
  s <- species[i]
  g <- genomes[i]

  # Read in variant impact counts
  varcounts <- read.table(
    paste0(
      "../analyses/results/datasets/historical-",
      s,
      "-vg-notrans/analyses/burden/historical-",
      s,
      "-vg-notrans.",
      g,
      "_all.dp6_allsites-filts.filtered_mindp5-biallelic-jointcall_allbal0.21-0.79.notrans.fmiss0.3.varimpacts_anc.tsv"
    ),
    header = TRUE
  )

  froh <- fread(
    paste0(
      "../analyses/results/datasets/historical-",
      s,
      "-vg-notrans/plots/inbreeding/historical-",
      s,
      "-vg-notrans.",
      g,
      "_all.dp6_allsites-filts.filtered_mindp5-biallelic-jointcall_allbal0.21-0.79.notrans.fmiss0.3.bcftools.ind_froh.tsv"
    ),
    header = TRUE,
    sep = "\t",
    select = c("sample", "population", "time", "depth", "Froh")
  )
  varcounts <- merge(varcounts, froh, by = c("sample", "population", "time", "depth"))
  varcounts$species <- s
  froh$species <- s
  froh_all <- rbind(froh_all, froh)
  varcounts_all <- rbind(varcounts_all, varcounts)
}

varcounts_all$year <- str_sub(varcounts_all$population, -4, -1)
varcounts_all$region <- str_sub(varcounts_all$population, 1, -5)

varcounts_all$species <- factor(
  varcounts_all$species,
  levels = species,
  labels = c("Po. icarus", "Pl. argus", "Cy. semiargus")
)

varcounts_all$time <- factor(
  varcounts_all$time,
  levels = c("historical", "modern"),
  labels = c("Historical", "Modern")
)

varcounts_all$region <- factor(
  varcounts_all$region,
  levels = c("WSkane", "SWSkane", "ESkane", "SESkane", "NSmaland", "Oland"),
  labels = c(
    "W Skåne", "SW Skåne", "E Skåne", "SE Skåne", "Småland", "Öland"
  )
)

varcounts_all$region_group <- varcounts_all$region
varcounts_all[varcounts_all$region_group == "SW Skåne", ]$region_group <- "W Skåne"
varcounts_all[varcounts_all$region_group == "SE Skåne", ]$region_group <- "E Skåne"

# perform linear models for derived count as a response to time period across
# relevant categories of mutations. these include putatively deleterious
# categories (high impact, moderate impact, conserved) as well as putatively
# neutral categories (low impact, intergenic) as a control. always normalize
# by total genotype count (nsites)
varcounts_stats <- c()

for (s in species_names) {
  for (i in c("gerp_n", "high", "mod", "low", "inter", "gerp_hom_n", "high_hom", "mod_hom", "low_hom", "inter_hom")) {
    hist <- mean(varcounts_all[varcounts_all$species == s & varcounts_all$time == "Historical", i] * 1000 / varcounts_all[varcounts_all$species == s & varcounts_all$time == "Historical", "nsites"])
    mod <- mean(varcounts_all[varcounts_all$species == s & varcounts_all$time == "Modern", i] * 1000 / varcounts_all[varcounts_all$species == s & varcounts_all$time == "Modern", "nsites"])
    ratio <- mod / hist
    model <- lme(as.formula(paste0(i, " * 1000 / nsites ~ time")),
      random = ~ 1 | region_group,
      data = varcounts_all[varcounts_all$species == s, ]
    )
    tidyed <- tidy(model, conf.int = TRUE, effects = "fixed")
    tidydf <- tidyed[2, c(3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9)]
    tidydf$hist.mean <- hist
    jackknife <- quantile(jackknife(varcounts_all[varcounts_all$species == s & varcounts_all$time == "Historical", i] * 1000 / varcounts_all[varcounts_all$species == s & varcounts_all$time == "Historical", "nsites"], mean)$jack.values, c(0.025, 0.975))
    tidydf$hist.low.jk.ci <- jackknife[1]
    tidydf$hist.high.jk.ci <- jackknife[2]
    tidydf$mod.mean <- mod
    jackknife <- quantile(jackknife(varcounts_all[varcounts_all$species == s & varcounts_all$time == "Modern", i] * 1000 / varcounts_all[varcounts_all$species == s & varcounts_all$time == "Modern", "nsites"], mean)$jack.values, c(0.025, 0.975))
    tidydf$mod.low.jk.ci <- jackknife[1]
    tidydf$mod.high.jk.ci <- jackknife[2]
    tidydf$`mod/hist` <- ratio
    tidydf <- round(tidydf, 5)
    tidydf$species <- s
    tidydf <- tidydf[, c(14, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 4)]
    tidydf$type <- i
    varcounts_stats <- rbind(varcounts_stats, tidydf)
  }
}

Inbreeding coefficients partitiond by RoH size
To visualize how much of the inbreeding coefficient was composed by runs of homozygosity by different lengths, we plotted them as bars colored by the proportion coming from different size classes.

  "inform_sites", "phred"

# exclude ROH < 200kb and < 30 Pherd score
rohs <- rohs[rohs$length >= 200000 & rohs$phred >= 30, ]

nroh <- rohs %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  summarise(cumroh = sum(length), nroh = n())

inds <- read.table(
  "../analyses/results/datasets/historical-csemiargus-vg-notrans/poplists/historical-csemiargus-vg-notrans_all.indiv.list",
  header = TRUE
)

# drop uncalled sample from ind list for sample looping
inds <- inds[inds$sample != "MZLU152765", ]

nroh <- merge(inds, nroh, by = "sample", all = TRUE)
nroh[is.na(nroh)] <- 0

norun <- c()
norun$type <- rep("RG", nrow(inds))
norun$sample <- inds$sample
norun$chr <- rep(0, nrow(inds))
norun$start <- rep(0, nrow(inds))
norun$end <- rep(0, nrow(inds))
norun$length <- rep(0, nrow(inds))
norun$inform_sites <- rep(0, nrow(inds))
norun$phred <- rep(0, nrow(inds))
norun <- data.frame(norun)

# set total autosomal length for C. semiargus
autosize <- 416794061

# prepare size bins to loop over
bins <- c(Inf, 6000000, 3000000, 1500000, 500000, 200000)

frohs <- c()
ranges <- c()

# loop over bins, quantifying Froh for that size bin in each sample
for (i in seq(length(bins))) {
  if (i <= length(bins) - 1) {
    runs <- rohs[rohs$length < bins[i], ]
    runs <- runs[runs$length >= bins[i + 1], ]
    runs <- rbind(runs, norun)
    runs <- runs %>%
      group_by(sample) %>%
      summarize(length = sum(length))
    runs <- merge(runs, inds, by = "sample")
    runs$froh <- runs$length / autosize
    runs$range <- paste0(bins[i], "-", bins[i + 1])
    ranges <- c(ranges, paste0(bins[i], "-", bins[i + 1]))
    frohs <- rbind(frohs, runs)
  }
}

species <- c("picarus", "pargus", "csemiargus")

title: Population structure
text:
PCA
Plot the outputs of a principal component analysis for each species together. This is used for making panel A of Figure 2 and as written makes the lower panel of Figure S4. To generate the upper panel of Figure S4, I ran the same code block, but exchanged the path for the covariance matrix to point to the bwa aln aligned dataset instead.

regs <- c("WSkane", "SWSkane", "ESkane", "SESkane", "NSmaland", "Oland")
regs_named <- c(
  "W Skåne", "SW Skåne", "E Skåne", "SE Skåne", "Småland",
  "Öland"
)
regs_cols <- c("#244F6E", "#244F6E", "#658399", "#658399", "#8A2A3B", "#fecd03")

pcas <- list()

# read in PCAngsd covariance results and compute PCs
for (i in c(1:length(species))) {
  s <- species[i]
  g <- genomes[i]
  cov <- as.matrix(read.table(
    paste0(
      "../analyses/results/datasets/historical-",
      s,
      "-vg-notrans/analyses/pcangsd/historical-",
      s,
      "-vg-notrans.",
      g,
      "_all_excl_pca-admix.dp8_allsites-filts.cov"
    ),
    header = FALSE,
  ))
  pop <- fread(
    paste0(
      "../analyses/results/datasets/historical-",
      s,
      "-vg-notrans/poplists/historical-",
      s,
      "-vg-notrans_all_excl_pca-admix.dp8.indiv.list"
    ),
    header = TRUE,
    sep = "\t",
    select = c("sample", "population", "time")
  )
  e <- eigen(cov)
  pc_var <- round((e$values / sum(e$values)) * 100, 2)
  pc <- data.frame(e$vectors)
  pc$sample <- pop$sample
  pc <- merge(pc, pop, by = "sample")
  pc$species <- s
  pc$region <- str_sub(pc$population, 1, -5)
  species_regs_index <- match(unique(pc$region), regs)
  species_regs <- regs[species_regs_index]
  species_regs_names <- regs_named[species_regs_index]
  species_regs_colors <- regs_cols[species_regs_index]

  pc$species <- factor(
    pc$species,
    levels = species,
    labels = c("Po. icarus", "Pl. argus", "Cy. semiargus")
  )

  pc$time <- factor(
    pc$time,
    levels = c("modern", "historical"),
    labels = c("Modern", "Historical")
  )

  pc$region <- factor(
    pc$region,
    levels = species_regs,
    labels = species_regs_names
  )

# make a ggplot for the PCA of each species
  pcas[[s]] <- ggplot(pc, aes(
    x = X1, y = X2, color = region, shape = time,
    fill = region
  )) +
    facet_grid(cols = vars(species)) +
    geom_point(size = 4, stroke = 1) +
    scale_shape_manual(
      values = c(21, 24)
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = species_regs_colors,
      name = "Geographic Region"
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = alpha(species_regs_colors, 0.7)
    ) +
    xlab(paste0("PC1 (", pc_var[1], "%)")) +
    ylab(paste0("PC2 (", pc_var[2], "%)")) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      strip.text.x = element_text(size = 10, face = "italic"),
      legend.position = "none",
      aspect.ratio = 1
    )
}

# make combined plot of all three species pcas
pcas <- plot_grid(

  pcas[["pargus"]],
  pcas[["csemiargus"]],
  ncol = 3, nrow = 1
)
